title: A longer diffracting wavelength
hook: Change wavelength and predict small-angle first-minimum angle.
misconception: small-angle first-minimum angle stays fixed when wavelength doubles.
objective: Apply θ ≈ λ/a to compare small-angle first-minimum angle when wavelength changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a single slit in the small-angle limit with fixed slit width, θ ≈ λ/a. When wavelength doubles, small-angle first-minimum angle becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model θ ≈ λ/a; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a single slit in the small-angle limit with fixed slit width, with a nonzero initial result. If wavelength triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on small-angle first-minimum angle?
recall.why: Apply θ ≈ λ/a under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
